newsitem.title: GERMANY: German communist-backed state govt survives vote.
newsitem.headline: German communist-backed state govt survives vote.

text.p: A minority government in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, the only state legislature which relies on the tacit support of former communists, survived a no-confidence vote on Tuesday.
The eastern state has been run by a controversial coalition of opposition Social Democrats and Greens since 1994.
It is the first and only state government in Germany to be aided by the Party of Democratic Socialism, the third strongest party in eastern Germany but virtually non-existent in the west.

The fate of the unusual coalition has been closely followed in Bonn because the so-called "Magdeburger Model" may be a way for the Social Democrats (SPD) to come to power after the next general election, due in 1998.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) failed to dislodge the minority "red-green" government, losing the vote by 59-38.

"The decision in Magdeburg today strikes a blow against job creation and the economic development of Saxony-Anhalt," said CDU General Secretary Peter Hintze in a statement in Bonn. "This leftist formation of SPD, Greens and communists...is also a threat for all of Germany."
